start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: a night at the fish market

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of a night at the fish market.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` is 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `That means nothing here.`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: east, west, south      (the room's exits in this fixed order: east, west, south, north; `Exits: none` if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `There is no exit that way.`. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/adventure.js`:

```
function adventure(world, script)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  There is no exit that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

Run the visible tests with `node --test test/*.test.js`.

require 'set'

module Adventure
  DIRS = ["north", "south", "east", "west"]
  SHOW = ["east", "south", "north", "west"]
  HAS_ITEMS = false
  HAS_LOCKS = false
  HAS_DARK = false
  HAS_UNDO = false
  HANDS = 2
  M_NOWAY = "There is no exit that way."
  M_LOCKED = "The door is locked."
  M_NOITEM = "There is no {X} here."
  M_NOHAVE = "No {X} in your pack."
  M_FULL = "You cannot carry more."
  M_DARK = "Pitch black."
  M_DARKTAKE = "It is too dark to find anything."
  M_UNKNOWN = "That means nothing here."
  M_TAKEN = "You pick it up."
  M_DROPPED = "Done."
  LOW = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
  DG = '0123456789'

  class Err < StandardError; end

  def self.good_id?(s)
    return false if s.length < 1 || s.length > 10 || !LOW.include?(s[0])
    s.each_char { |c| return false unless (LOW + DG + '_').include?(c) }
    true
  end

  def self.good_text?(s, mx)
    return false if s.length < 1 || s.length > mx || s[0] == ' ' || s[-1] == ' '
    s.each_char { |c| return false if c < ' ' || c > '~' }
    true
  end

  def self.good_num?(s)
    return false if s.length < 1 || s.length > 3
    s.each_char { |c| return false unless DG.include?(c) }
    s.length == 1 || s[0] != '0'
  end

  def self.directives
    d = { 'room' => %w[id text40], 'desc' => %w[id text120], 'exit' => %w[id dir id], 'start' => %w[id] }
    d['item'] = %w[id id text40] if HAS_ITEMS
    d['lock'] = %w[id dir id] if HAS_LOCKS
    if HAS_DARK
      d['dark'] = %w[id]
      d['light'] = %w[id]
      d['value'] = %w[id num]
      d['vault'] = %w[id]
    end
    d
  end

  def self.parse_world(text)
    spec = directives
    w = { rooms: {}, desc: {}, exits: {}, start: nil, items: {}, locks: {}, dark: Set.new, light: Set.new, value: {}, vault: Set.new }
    refs = []
    seen_start = false
    text.split("\n", -1).each_with_index do |line, ln|
      n = ln + 1
      next if line.empty?
      kw = line.split(/ /, 2)[0]
      raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" unless spec.key?(kw)
      kinds = spec[kw]
      parts = kinds[-1].start_with?('text') ? line.split(/ /, kinds.length + 1) : line.split(/ /, -1)
      raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if parts.length != 1 + kinds.length
      args = parts[1..-1]
      kinds.each_with_index do |kind, i|
        a = args[i]
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: id" if kind == 'id' && !good_id?(a)
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if kind == 'dir' && !DIRS.include?(a)
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if kind == 'num' && !good_num?(a)
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if kind.start_with?('text') && !good_text?(a, kind[4..-1].to_i)
      end
      dup = false
      r = []
      case kw
      when 'room'
        dup = w[:rooms].key?(args[0])
        w[:rooms][args[0]] = args[1]
      when 'desc'
        dup = w[:desc].key?(args[0])
        w[:desc][args[0]] = args[1]
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      when 'exit'
        k = "#{args[0]} #{args[1]}"
        dup = w[:exits].key?(k)
        w[:exits][k] = args[2]
        r = [['room', args[0]], ['room', args[2]]]
      when 'start'
        dup = seen_start
        seen_start = true
        w[:start] = args[0]
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      when 'item'
        dup = w[:items].key?(args[0])
        w[:items][args[0]] = [args[1], args[2]]
        r = [['room', args[1]]]
      when 'lock'
        k = "#{args[0]} #{args[1]}"
        dup = w[:locks].key?(k)
        w[:locks][k] = args[2]
        r = [['exit', k], ['item', args[2]]]
      when 'dark'
        dup = w[:dark].include?(args[0])
        w[:dark].add(args[0])
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      when 'light'
        dup = w[:light].include?(args[0])
        w[:light].add(args[0])
        r = [['item', args[0]]]
      when 'value'
        dup = w[:value].key?(args[0])
        w[:value][args[0]] = args[1].to_i
        r = [['item', args[0]]]
      when 'vault'
        dup = w[:vault].include?(args[0])
        w[:vault].add(args[0])
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      end
      raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: duplicate" if dup
      refs << [n, r]
    end
    refs.each do |n, r|
      r.each do |ref|
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: unknown" if ref[0] == 'room' && !w[:rooms].key?(ref[1])
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: unknown" if ref[0] == 'item' && !w[:items].key?(ref[1])
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: unknown" if ref[0] == 'exit' && !w[:exits].key?(ref[1])
      end
    end
    raise Err, 'error: world: no start' if w[:start].nil?
    w
  end

  def self.lit_room?(w, st)
    return true unless HAS_DARK
    !w[:dark].include?(st[:loc]) || st[:inv].any? { |i| w[:light].include?(i) }
  end

  def self.view(w, st)
    return [M_DARK] unless lit_room?(w, st)
    loc = st[:loc]
    out = ["== #{w[:rooms][loc]} =="]
    out << w[:desc][loc] if w[:desc].key?(loc)
    ex = SHOW.select { |d| w[:exits].key?("#{loc} #{d}") }
    out << ('Exits: ' + (ex.empty? ? 'none' : ex.join(', ')))
    here = st[:here][loc]
    out << ('Items: ' + here.to_a.sort.join(', ')) if HAS_ITEMS && !here.empty?
    out
  end

  def self.snap(st)
    here = {}
    st[:here].each { |k, v| here[k] = v.dup }
    { loc: st[:loc], inv: st[:inv].dup, here: here, turns: st[:turns] }
  end

  def self.adventure(world, script)
    begin
      w = parse_world(world)
    rescue Err => e
      return e.message
    end
    st = { loc: w[:start], inv: Set.new, here: {}, turns: 0 }
    w[:rooms].each_key { |r| st[:here][r] = Set.new }
    w[:items].each { |name, (room, _)| st[:here][room].add(name) }
    undo = []
    saves = {}
    out = []
    script.split("\n", -1).each do |cmd|
      next if cmd.empty?
      out << "> #{cmd}"
      ws = cmd.split(/ /, -1)
      v = ws[0]
      res = nil
      if v == 'look' && ws.length == 1
        res = view(w, st)
      elsif v == 'go' && ws.length == 2 && DIRS.include?(ws[1])
        key = "#{st[:loc]} #{ws[1]}"
        tgt = w[:exits][key]
        if tgt.nil?
          res = [M_NOWAY]
        elsif HAS_LOCKS && w[:locks].key?(key) && !st[:inv].include?(w[:locks][key])
          res = [M_LOCKED]
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st[:loc] = tgt
          st[:turns] += 1
          res = view(w, st)
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'take' && ws.length == 2
        if !lit_room?(w, st)
          res = [M_DARKTAKE]
        elsif !st[:here][st[:loc]].include?(ws[1])
          res = [M_NOITEM.gsub('{X}') { ws[1] }]
        elsif st[:inv].size >= HANDS
          res = [M_FULL]
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st[:here][st[:loc]].delete(ws[1])
          st[:inv].add(ws[1])
          res = [M_TAKEN]
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'drop' && ws.length == 2
        if !st[:inv].include?(ws[1])
          res = [M_NOHAVE.gsub('{X}') { ws[1] }]
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st[:inv].delete(ws[1])
          st[:here][st[:loc]].add(ws[1])
          res = [M_DROPPED]
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'examine' && ws.length == 2
        if st[:inv].include?(ws[1]) || (lit_room?(w, st) && st[:here][st[:loc]].include?(ws[1]))
          res = [w[:items][ws[1]][1]]
        else
          res = [M_NOITEM.gsub('{X}') { ws[1] }]
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'inv' && ws.length == 1
        res = st[:inv].empty? ? ['You carry nothing.'] : ['You carry: ' + st[:inv].to_a.sort.join(', ')]
      elsif HAS_DARK && v == 'score' && ws.length == 1
        tot = 0
        w[:vault].each { |r| st[:here][r].each { |i| tot += w[:value][i] || 0 } }
        res = ["Score: #{tot}"]
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'undo' && ws.length == 1
        if undo.empty?
          res = ['Nothing to undo.']
        else
          s = undo.pop
          st.merge!(s)
          res = ['Undone.']
        end
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'turns' && ws.length == 1
        res = ["Turns: #{st[:turns]}"]
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'save' && ws.length == 2 && good_id?(ws[1])
        saves[ws[1]] = snap(st)
        res = ['Saved.']
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'load' && ws.length == 2 && good_id?(ws[1])
        if !saves.key?(ws[1])
          res = ['No such save.']
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st.merge!(snap(saves[ws[1]]))
          res = ['Loaded.']
        end
      else
        res = [M_UNKNOWN]
      end
      out.concat(res)
    end
    out.join("\n")
  end
end

start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: the harbour office after hours

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of the harbour office after hours.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` is 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `That means nothing here.`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: east, south, north      (the room's exits in this fixed order: east, south, north, west; `Exits: none` if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `There is no exit that way.`. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/adventure.rb` (module `Adventure`):

```
Adventure.adventure(world, script)
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  There is no exit that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

Run the visible tests with `ruby -Ilib -Itest test/test_adventure.rb`.

start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: the harbour office after hours

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of the harbour office after hours.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)
    item NAME ROOM TEXT    an item that starts out lying in ROOM; TEXT is what `examine` shows

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` and item `TEXT` are 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`; an item name used twice.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text, every item `NAME` by an `item` line.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room carrying nothing and may carry at most 4 items. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |
| `take NAME` | picks an item up from the room |
| `drop NAME` | puts a carried item down in the room |
| `examine NAME` | shows the item's `TEXT`; works for a carried item, or for an item lying in the room (not when the room is dark) |
| `inv` | lists what the player carries |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `Pardon?`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: west, south, east      (the room's exits in this fixed order: west, south, east, north; `Exits: none` if there are none)
Items: a, b                (items lying here, ascending byte order; the line is left out if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `Nothing but wall that way.`. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

`take NAME`, checked in this order: if the item is not lying in this room: `No {X} in sight.` (`{X}` is replaced by the name as typed, whatever it is); if the player already carries 4 items: `You cannot carry more.`; otherwise the item moves to the player and the response is `You pick it up.`. `drop NAME`: if the player does not carry it `No {X} in your pack.` (again with `{X}` replaced), otherwise it is left in the current room and the response is `Done.`. `examine NAME` with an item that is neither carried nor visible: `No {X} in sight.`. `inv`: `You carry: a, b` (ascending byte order) or `You carry nothing.`

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Adventure.java` (class `Adventure`, default package):

```
public static String adventure(String world, String script)
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  Nothing but wall that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

**Example 2**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item rope yard a coil of rope
script:
  take lamp
  examine lamp
  go north
  look
  take rope
  inv
  drop lamp
result:
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > examine lamp
  a brass lamp
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > take rope
  You pick it up.
  > inv
  You carry: lamp, rope
  > drop lamp
  Done.
```

start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: the boatyard at dusk

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of the boatyard at dusk.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)
    item NAME ROOM TEXT    an item that starts out lying in ROOM; TEXT is what `examine` shows

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` and item `TEXT` are 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`; an item name used twice.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text, every item `NAME` by an `item` line.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room carrying nothing and may carry at most 3 items. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |
| `take NAME` | picks an item up from the room |
| `drop NAME` | puts a carried item down in the room |
| `examine NAME` | shows the item's `TEXT`; works for a carried item, or for an item lying in the room (not when the room is dark) |
| `inv` | lists what the player carries |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `Pardon?`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: west, south, east      (the room's exits in this fixed order: west, south, east, north; `Exits: none` if there are none)
Items: a, b                (items lying here, ascending byte order; the line is left out if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `There is no exit that way.`. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

`take NAME`, checked in this order: if the item is not lying in this room: `There is no {X} here.` (`{X}` is replaced by the name as typed, whatever it is); if the player already carries 3 items: `Too much to carry.`; otherwise the item moves to the player and the response is `You pick it up.`. `drop NAME`: if the player does not carry it `You aren't carrying {X}.` (again with `{X}` replaced), otherwise it is left in the current room and the response is `Done.`. `examine NAME` with an item that is neither carried nor visible: `There is no {X} here.`. `inv`: `You carry: a, b` (ascending byte order) or `You carry nothing.`

## Interface

Implement this function in `adventure.go` (package `adventure`, module `example.com/adventure`):

```
func Adventure(world, script string) string
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  There is no exit that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

**Example 2**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item rope yard a coil of rope
script:
  take lamp
  examine lamp
  go north
  look
  take rope
  inv
  drop lamp
result:
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > examine lamp
  a brass lamp
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > take rope
  You pick it up.
  > inv
  You carry: lamp, rope
  > drop lamp
  Done.
```

require 'set'

module Adventure
  DIRS = ["north", "south", "east", "west", "up", "down"]
  SHOW = ["south", "up", "north", "west", "east", "down"]
  HAS_ITEMS = true
  HAS_LOCKS = true
  HAS_DARK = false
  HAS_UNDO = false
  HANDS = 4
  M_NOWAY = "Nothing but wall that way."
  M_LOCKED = "A lock bars the way."
  M_NOITEM = "No {X} in sight."
  M_NOHAVE = "You have no {X}."
  M_FULL = "You cannot carry more."
  M_DARK = "You see nothing in the dark."
  M_DARKTAKE = "Too dark to reach for anything."
  M_UNKNOWN = "That means nothing here."
  M_TAKEN = "Done."
  M_DROPPED = "You put it down."
  LOW = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
  DG = '0123456789'

  class Err < StandardError; end

  def self.good_id?(s)
    return false if s.length < 1 || s.length > 10 || !LOW.include?(s[0])
    s.each_char { |c| return false unless (LOW + DG + '_').include?(c) }
    true
  end

  def self.good_text?(s, mx)
    return false if s.length < 1 || s.length > mx || s[0] == ' ' || s[-1] == ' '
    s.each_char { |c| return false if c < ' ' || c > '~' }
    true
  end

  def self.good_num?(s)
    return false if s.length < 1 || s.length > 3
    s.each_char { |c| return false unless DG.include?(c) }
    s.length == 1 || s[0] != '0'
  end

  def self.directives
    d = { 'room' => %w[id text40], 'desc' => %w[id text120], 'exit' => %w[id dir id], 'start' => %w[id] }
    d['item'] = %w[id id text40] if HAS_ITEMS
    d['lock'] = %w[id dir id] if HAS_LOCKS
    if HAS_DARK
      d['dark'] = %w[id]
      d['light'] = %w[id]
      d['value'] = %w[id num]
      d['vault'] = %w[id]
    end
    d
  end

  def self.parse_world(text)
    spec = directives
    w = { rooms: {}, desc: {}, exits: {}, start: nil, items: {}, locks: {}, dark: Set.new, light: Set.new, value: {}, vault: Set.new }
    refs = []
    seen_start = false
    text.split("\n", -1).each_with_index do |line, ln|
      n = ln + 1
      next if line.empty?
      kw = line.split(/ /, 2)[0]
      raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" unless spec.key?(kw)
      kinds = spec[kw]
      parts = kinds[-1].start_with?('text') ? line.split(/ /, kinds.length + 1) : line.split(/ /, -1)
      raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if parts.length != 1 + kinds.length
      args = parts[1..-1]
      kinds.each_with_index do |kind, i|
        a = args[i]
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: id" if kind == 'id' && !good_id?(a)
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if kind == 'dir' && !DIRS.include?(a)
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if kind == 'num' && !good_num?(a)
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: syntax" if kind.start_with?('text') && !good_text?(a, kind[4..-1].to_i)
      end
      dup = false
      r = []
      case kw
      when 'room'
        dup = w[:rooms].key?(args[0])
        w[:rooms][args[0]] = args[1]
      when 'desc'
        dup = w[:desc].key?(args[0])
        w[:desc][args[0]] = args[1]
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      when 'exit'
        k = "#{args[0]} #{args[1]}"
        dup = w[:exits].key?(k)
        w[:exits][k] = args[2]
        r = [['room', args[0]], ['room', args[2]]]
      when 'start'
        dup = seen_start
        seen_start = true
        w[:start] = args[0]
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      when 'item'
        dup = w[:items].key?(args[0])
        w[:items][args[0]] = [args[1], args[2]]
        r = [['room', args[1]]]
      when 'lock'
        k = "#{args[0]} #{args[1]}"
        dup = w[:locks].key?(k)
        w[:locks][k] = args[2]
        r = [['exit', k], ['item', args[2]]]
      when 'dark'
        dup = w[:dark].include?(args[0])
        w[:dark].add(args[0])
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      when 'light'
        dup = w[:light].include?(args[0])
        w[:light].add(args[0])
        r = [['item', args[0]]]
      when 'value'
        dup = w[:value].key?(args[0])
        w[:value][args[0]] = args[1].to_i
        r = [['item', args[0]]]
      when 'vault'
        dup = w[:vault].include?(args[0])
        w[:vault].add(args[0])
        r = [['room', args[0]]]
      end
      raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: duplicate" if dup
      refs << [n, r]
    end
    refs.each do |n, r|
      r.each do |ref|
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: unknown" if ref[0] == 'room' && !w[:rooms].key?(ref[1])
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: unknown" if ref[0] == 'item' && !w[:items].key?(ref[1])
        raise Err, "error: world line #{n}: unknown" if ref[0] == 'exit' && !w[:exits].key?(ref[1])
      end
    end
    raise Err, 'error: world: no start' if w[:start].nil?
    w
  end

  def self.lit_room?(w, st)
    return true unless HAS_DARK
    !w[:dark].include?(st[:loc]) || st[:inv].any? { |i| w[:light].include?(i) }
  end

  def self.view(w, st)
    return [M_DARK] unless lit_room?(w, st)
    loc = st[:loc]
    out = ["== #{w[:rooms][loc]} =="]
    out << w[:desc][loc] if w[:desc].key?(loc)
    ex = SHOW.select { |d| w[:exits].key?("#{loc} #{d}") }
    out << ('Exits: ' + (ex.empty? ? 'none' : ex.join(', ')))
    here = st[:here][loc]
    out << ('Items: ' + here.to_a.sort.join(', ')) if HAS_ITEMS && !here.empty?
    out
  end

  def self.snap(st)
    here = {}
    st[:here].each { |k, v| here[k] = v.dup }
    { loc: st[:loc], inv: st[:inv].dup, here: here, turns: st[:turns] }
  end

  def self.adventure(world, script)
    begin
      w = parse_world(world)
    rescue Err => e
      return e.message
    end
    st = { loc: w[:start], inv: Set.new, here: {}, turns: 0 }
    w[:rooms].each_key { |r| st[:here][r] = Set.new }
    w[:items].each { |name, (room, _)| st[:here][room].add(name) }
    undo = []
    saves = {}
    out = []
    script.split("\n", -1).each do |cmd|
      next if cmd.empty?
      out << "> #{cmd}"
      ws = cmd.split(/ /, -1)
      v = ws[0]
      res = nil
      if v == 'look' && ws.length == 1
        res = view(w, st)
      elsif v == 'go' && ws.length == 2 && DIRS.include?(ws[1])
        key = "#{st[:loc]} #{ws[1]}"
        tgt = w[:exits][key]
        if tgt.nil?
          res = [M_NOWAY]
        elsif HAS_LOCKS && w[:locks].key?(key) && !st[:inv].include?(w[:locks][key])
          res = [M_LOCKED]
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st[:loc] = tgt
          st[:turns] += 1
          res = view(w, st)
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'take' && ws.length == 2
        if !lit_room?(w, st)
          res = [M_DARKTAKE]
        elsif !st[:here][st[:loc]].include?(ws[1])
          res = [M_NOITEM.gsub('{X}') { ws[1] }]
        elsif st[:inv].size >= HANDS
          res = [M_FULL]
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st[:here][st[:loc]].delete(ws[1])
          st[:inv].add(ws[1])
          res = [M_TAKEN]
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'drop' && ws.length == 2
        if !st[:inv].include?(ws[1])
          res = [M_NOHAVE.gsub('{X}') { ws[1] }]
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st[:inv].delete(ws[1])
          st[:here][st[:loc]].add(ws[1])
          res = [M_DROPPED]
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'examine' && ws.length == 2
        if st[:inv].include?(ws[1]) || (lit_room?(w, st) && st[:here][st[:loc]].include?(ws[1]))
          res = [w[:items][ws[1]][1]]
        else
          res = [M_NOITEM.gsub('{X}') { ws[1] }]
        end
      elsif HAS_ITEMS && v == 'inv' && ws.length == 1
        res = st[:inv].empty? ? ['You carry nothing.'] : ['You carry: ' + st[:inv].to_a.sort.join(', ')]
      elsif HAS_DARK && v == 'score' && ws.length == 1
        tot = 0
        w[:vault].each { |r| st[:here][r].each { |i| tot += w[:value][i] || 0 } }
        res = ["Score: #{tot}"]
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'undo' && ws.length == 1
        if undo.empty?
          res = ['Nothing to undo.']
        else
          s = undo.pop
          st.merge!(s)
          res = ['Undone.']
        end
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'turns' && ws.length == 1
        res = ["Turns: #{st[:turns]}"]
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'save' && ws.length == 2 && good_id?(ws[1])
        saves[ws[1]] = snap(st)
        res = ['Saved.']
      elsif HAS_UNDO && v == 'load' && ws.length == 2 && good_id?(ws[1])
        if !saves.key?(ws[1])
          res = ['No such save.']
        else
          undo << snap(st)
          st.merge!(snap(saves[ws[1]]))
          res = ['Loaded.']
        end
      else
        res = [M_UNKNOWN]
      end
      out.concat(res)
    end
    out.join("\n")
  end
end

start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: the boatyard at dusk

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of the boatyard at dusk.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)
    item NAME ROOM TEXT    an item that starts out lying in ROOM; TEXT is what `examine` shows
    lock ROOM DIR KEY      the exit DIR of ROOM can only be used while the player carries the item KEY

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`, `up`, `down`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` and item `TEXT` are 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`; an item name used twice; two `lock` lines for the same `ROOM` and `DIR`.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text, every item `NAME` by an `item` line, and a `lock` must name an existing `exit`.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room carrying nothing and may carry at most 4 items. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |
| `take NAME` | picks an item up from the room |
| `drop NAME` | puts a carried item down in the room |
| `examine NAME` | shows the item's `TEXT`; works for a carried item, or for an item lying in the room (not when the room is dark) |
| `inv` | lists what the player carries |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `That means nothing here.`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: south, up, north      (the room's exits in this fixed order: south, up, north, west, east, down; `Exits: none` if there are none)
Items: a, b                (items lying here, ascending byte order; the line is left out if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `Nothing but wall that way.`. If the exit is locked and the player does not carry its key it is `A lock bars the way.` (nothing changes); the key is not used up. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

`take NAME`, checked in this order: if the item is not lying in this room: `No {X} in sight.` (`{X}` is replaced by the name as typed, whatever it is); if the player already carries 4 items: `You cannot carry more.`; otherwise the item moves to the player and the response is `Done.`. `drop NAME`: if the player does not carry it `You have no {X}.` (again with `{X}` replaced), otherwise it is left in the current room and the response is `You put it down.`. `examine NAME` with an item that is neither carried nor visible: `No {X} in sight.`. `inv`: `You carry: a, b` (ascending byte order) or `You carry nothing.`

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/adventure.rb` (module `Adventure`):

```
Adventure.adventure(world, script)
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  Nothing but wall that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

**Example 2**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item rope yard a coil of rope
script:
  take lamp
  examine lamp
  go north
  look
  take rope
  inv
  drop lamp
result:
  > take lamp
  Done.
  > examine lamp
  a brass lamp
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > take rope
  Done.
  > inv
  You carry: lamp, rope
  > drop lamp
  You put it down.
```

**Example 3**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room vault Vault
  exit hall east vault
  exit vault west hall
  item key hall an iron key
  lock hall east key
  start hall
script:
  go east
  take key
  go east
  drop key
  go west
  go east
result:
  > go east
  A lock bars the way.
  > take key
  Done.
  > go east
  == Vault ==
  Exits: west
  > drop key
  You put it down.
  > go west
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: east
  > go east
  A lock bars the way.
```

# Text adventure engine: a night at the fish market

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of a night at the fish market.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)
    item NAME ROOM TEXT    an item that starts out lying in ROOM; TEXT is what `examine` shows
    lock ROOM DIR KEY      the exit DIR of ROOM can only be used while the player carries the item KEY
    dark ID                the room is dark
    light NAME             this item is a light source
    value NAME N           the item is worth N points
    vault ID               items lying in this room score

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`, `up`, `down`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` and item `TEXT` are 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.
* `N` is a decimal number from 1 to 999 without leading zeros.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`; an item name used twice; two `lock` lines for the same `ROOM` and `DIR`; a second `dark`, `light`, `value` or `vault` for the same room or item.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text, every item `NAME` by an `item` line, and a `lock` must name an existing `exit`.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room carrying nothing and may carry at most 4 items. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |
| `take NAME` | picks an item up from the room |
| `drop NAME` | puts a carried item down in the room |
| `examine NAME` | shows the item's `TEXT`; works for a carried item, or for an item lying in the room (not when the room is dark) |
| `inv` | lists what the player carries |
| `score` | shows the score |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `I don't understand.`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: down, north, south      (the room's exits in this fixed order: down, north, south, up, west, east; `Exits: none` if there are none)
Items: a, b                (items lying here, ascending byte order; the line is left out if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `There is no exit that way.`. If the exit is locked and the player does not carry its key it is `The door is locked.` (nothing changes); the key is not used up. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

`take NAME`, checked in this order: if the room is dark and the player carries no light source: `Too dark to reach for anything.`; if the item is not lying in this room: `No {X} in sight.` (`{X}` is replaced by the name as typed, whatever it is); if the player already carries 4 items: `Too much to carry.`; otherwise the item moves to the player and the response is `You pick it up.`. `drop NAME`: if the player does not carry it `You have no {X}.` (again with `{X}` replaced), otherwise it is left in the current room and the response is `Done.`. `examine NAME` with an item that is neither carried nor visible: `No {X} in sight.`. `inv`: `You carry: a, b` (ascending byte order) or `You carry nothing.`

**Darkness.** A dark room is *lit* when the player carries at least one light source (any item named by a `light` line); in a dark room that is not lit the room view is the single line `You see nothing in the dark.` (for `look` and after `go`). Moving is still allowed. `score` responds `Score: N`, where `N` is the sum of the `value`s of all items currently lying in the rooms named by `vault` lines (an item without a `value` counts 0).

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/Adventure.java` (class `Adventure`, default package):

```
public static String adventure(String world, String script)
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  There is no exit that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

**Example 2**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item rope yard a coil of rope
script:
  take lamp
  examine lamp
  go north
  look
  take rope
  inv
  drop lamp
result:
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > examine lamp
  a brass lamp
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > take rope
  You pick it up.
  > inv
  You carry: lamp, rope
  > drop lamp
  Done.
```

**Example 3**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room vault Vault
  exit hall east vault
  exit vault west hall
  item key hall an iron key
  lock hall east key
  start hall
script:
  go east
  take key
  go east
  drop key
  go west
  go east
result:
  > go east
  The door is locked.
  > take key
  You pick it up.
  > go east
  == Vault ==
  Exits: west
  > drop key
  Done.
  > go west
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: east
  > go east
  The door is locked.
```

**Example 4**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room cave Cave
  exit hall down cave
  exit cave up hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item coin cave a silver coin
  light lamp
  dark cave
  vault hall
  value coin 25
  start hall
script:
  go down
  look
  go up
  take lamp
  go down
  look
  take coin
  go up
  drop coin
  score
result:
  > go down
  You see nothing in the dark.
  > look
  You see nothing in the dark.
  > go up
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: down
  Items: lamp
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > go down
  == Cave ==
  Exits: up
  Items: coin
  > look
  == Cave ==
  Exits: up
  Items: coin
  > take coin
  You pick it up.
  > go up
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: down
  > drop coin
  Done.
  > score
  Score: 25
```

Run the visible tests with `mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain`.

start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: a night at the fish market

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of a night at the fish market.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)
    item NAME ROOM TEXT    an item that starts out lying in ROOM; TEXT is what `examine` shows
    lock ROOM DIR KEY      the exit DIR of ROOM can only be used while the player carries the item KEY
    dark ID                the room is dark
    light NAME             this item is a light source
    value NAME N           the item is worth N points
    vault ID               items lying in this room score

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`, `up`, `down`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` and item `TEXT` are 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.
* `N` is a decimal number from 1 to 999 without leading zeros.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`; an item name used twice; two `lock` lines for the same `ROOM` and `DIR`; a second `dark`, `light`, `value` or `vault` for the same room or item.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text, every item `NAME` by an `item` line, and a `lock` must name an existing `exit`.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room carrying nothing and may carry at most 4 items. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |
| `take NAME` | picks an item up from the room |
| `drop NAME` | puts a carried item down in the room |
| `examine NAME` | shows the item's `TEXT`; works for a carried item, or for an item lying in the room (not when the room is dark) |
| `inv` | lists what the player carries |
| `score` | shows the score |
| `undo` | takes back the last state change |
| `turns` | shows the move count |
| `save NAME` | remembers the current state under a name |
| `load NAME` | goes back to a saved state |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `Pardon?`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: east, north, south      (the room's exits in this fixed order: east, north, south, down, west, up; `Exits: none` if there are none)
Items: a, b                (items lying here, ascending byte order; the line is left out if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `You can't go that way.`. If the exit is locked and the player does not carry its key it is `A lock bars the way.` (nothing changes); the key is not used up. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

`take NAME`, checked in this order: if the room is dark and the player carries no light source: `It is too dark to find anything.`; if the item is not lying in this room: `You see no {X} here.` (`{X}` is replaced by the name as typed, whatever it is); if the player already carries 4 items: `Your hands are full.`; otherwise the item moves to the player and the response is `You pick it up.`. `drop NAME`: if the player does not carry it `No {X} in your pack.` (again with `{X}` replaced), otherwise it is left in the current room and the response is `Dropped.`. `examine NAME` with an item that is neither carried nor visible: `You see no {X} here.`. `inv`: `You carry: a, b` (ascending byte order) or `You carry nothing.`

**Darkness.** A dark room is *lit* when the player carries at least one light source (any item named by a `light` line); in a dark room that is not lit the room view is the single line `You see nothing in the dark.` (for `look` and after `go`). Moving is still allowed. `score` responds `Score: N`, where `N` is the sum of the `value`s of all items currently lying in the rooms named by `vault` lines (an item without a `value` counts 0).

**State, undo and saves.** The state is the player's room, the carried items, where every item lies, and the move count (the number of successful `go` commands). Every *successful* `go`, `take`, `drop` and `load` first remembers the state before it, on a stack. `undo` pops that stack and restores the state (`Undone.`); with an empty stack it responds `Nothing to undo.` and nothing else happens. `turns` responds `Turns: N`. `save NAME` stores the current state under NAME (overwriting an older save) and responds `Saved.`; `load NAME` responds `No such save.` if there is none, otherwise it remembers the current state on the undo stack, restores the saved one and responds `Loaded.` (the save itself stays). Failed commands, `look`, `inv`, `score`, `turns`, `save` and `undo` do not touch the stack.

## Interface

Implement this function in `adventure.go` (package `adventure`, module `example.com/adventure`):

```
func Adventure(world, script string) string
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  You can't go that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

**Example 2**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item rope yard a coil of rope
script:
  take lamp
  examine lamp
  go north
  look
  take rope
  inv
  drop lamp
result:
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > examine lamp
  a brass lamp
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > take rope
  You pick it up.
  > inv
  You carry: lamp, rope
  > drop lamp
  Dropped.
```

**Example 3**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room vault Vault
  exit hall east vault
  exit vault west hall
  item key hall an iron key
  lock hall east key
  start hall
script:
  go east
  take key
  go east
  drop key
  go west
  go east
result:
  > go east
  A lock bars the way.
  > take key
  You pick it up.
  > go east
  == Vault ==
  Exits: west
  > drop key
  Dropped.
  > go west
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: east
  > go east
  A lock bars the way.
```

**Example 4**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room cave Cave
  exit hall down cave
  exit cave up hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item coin cave a silver coin
  light lamp
  dark cave
  vault hall
  value coin 25
  start hall
script:
  go down
  look
  go up
  take lamp
  go down
  look
  take coin
  go up
  drop coin
  score
result:
  > go down
  You see nothing in the dark.
  > look
  You see nothing in the dark.
  > go up
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: down
  Items: lamp
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > go down
  == Cave ==
  Exits: up
  Items: coin
  > look
  == Cave ==
  Exits: up
  Items: coin
  > take coin
  You pick it up.
  > go up
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: down
  > drop coin
  Dropped.
  > score
  Score: 25
```

**Example 5**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  save here
  go north
  turns
  undo
  look
  go north
  load here
  turns
  undo
  turns
  undo
result:
  > save here
  Saved.
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > turns
  Turns: 1
  > undo
  Undone.
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > load here
  Loaded.
  > turns
  Turns: 0
  > undo
  Undone.
  > turns
  Turns: 1
  > undo
  Undone.
```

start.README.md:
# Text adventure engine: the harbour office after hours

`adventure(world, script)` builds a small world from a description, plays a script of commands on it and returns the transcript. The world is the setting of the harbour office after hours.

## The world description

`world` is text made of lines separated by `\n`. Empty lines are ignored (but they count when line numbers are reported). Every other line is one directive: a keyword and its arguments separated by **single spaces**:

    room ID TITLE          a room
    desc ID TEXT           the description shown in that room (optional, at most once per room)
    exit ID DIR TARGET     a one-way exit from room ID in direction DIR to room TARGET
    start ID               the room where the player begins (exactly one)
    item NAME ROOM TEXT    an item that starts out lying in ROOM; TEXT is what `examine` shows
    lock ROOM DIR KEY      the exit DIR of ROOM can only be used while the player carries the item KEY
    dark ID                the room is dark
    light NAME             this item is a light source
    value NAME N           the item is worth N points
    vault ID               items lying in this room score

* `ID` and item `NAME`: 1 to 10 characters, a lower-case ASCII letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or `_`.
* `DIR` is one of `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`, `up`, `down`.
* `TITLE` and `TEXT` are the **rest of the line** after the arguments before them: `TITLE` and item `TEXT` are 1 to 40 characters, `desc` text 1 to 120, printable ASCII (space to `~`), and neither starts nor ends with a space.
* `N` is a decimal number from 1 to 999 without leading zeros.

A world error stops everything: the result is just the error text, with no transcript. Errors are found in three passes:

1. line by line, the first line with `error: world line N: WHY`: `syntax` (unknown keyword, wrong number of words, a `DIR` that is not in the list, a `TITLE`/`TEXT`/number that breaks its rule), then `id` (an `ID` or `NAME` that is not valid; checked left to right in the line, together with the other word checks), then `duplicate` (see below).
   `duplicate` is reported for: a room defined twice; a second `desc` for a room; the same `ID` and `DIR` in two `exit` lines; a second `start`; an item name used twice; two `lock` lines for the same `ROOM` and `DIR`; a second `dark`, `light`, `value` or `vault` for the same room or item.
2. then, if pass 1 found nothing, in line order, the first line that refers to something that does not exist is `error: world line N: unknown`: every `ID` that names a room must be defined by a `room` line anywhere in the text, every item `NAME` by an `item` line, and a `lock` must name an existing `exit`.
3. finally `error: world: no start` if there is no `start` line.

## Playing

`script` is text made of lines separated by `\n`; empty lines are skipped. Each other line is a command, case-sensitive, words separated by single spaces. The player starts in the `start` room carrying nothing and may carry at most 2 items. The transcript has, for every command, the line `> ` followed by the command text exactly as written, then the response lines. Lines are joined with `\n` and there is no trailing newline (an empty script gives the empty text).

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `look` | shows the room (see below) |
| `go DIR` | moves through the exit and shows the new room |
| `take NAME` | picks an item up from the room |
| `drop NAME` | puts a carried item down in the room |
| `examine NAME` | shows the item's `TEXT`; works for a carried item, or for an item lying in the room (not when the room is dark) |
| `inv` | lists what the player carries |
| `score` | shows the score |
| `undo` | takes back the last state change |
| `turns` | shows the move count |
| `save NAME` | remembers the current state under a name |
| `load NAME` | goes back to a saved state |

A command with the wrong number of words (or with a `DIR` that is not in the list, or a `save`/`load` name that is not a valid `ID`) is not understood, and so is any other text: the response is the single line `I don't understand.`.

**Room view** (the response of `look`, and of a successful `go`):

```
== TITLE ==
TEXT of the desc line      (only if the room has one)
Exits: north, south, west      (the room's exits in this fixed order: north, south, west, east, up, down; `Exits: none` if there are none)
Items: a, b                (items lying here, ascending byte order; the line is left out if there are none)
```

`go DIR`: if the room has no exit that way the response is `You can't go that way.`. If the exit is locked and the player does not carry its key it is `The door is locked.` (nothing changes); the key is not used up. Otherwise the player moves and gets the room view of the new room.

`take NAME`, checked in this order: if the room is dark and the player carries no light source: `You fumble in the dark.`; if the item is not lying in this room: `There is no {X} here.` (`{X}` is replaced by the name as typed, whatever it is); if the player already carries 2 items: `Too much to carry.`; otherwise the item moves to the player and the response is `You pick it up.`. `drop NAME`: if the player does not carry it `No {X} in your pack.` (again with `{X}` replaced), otherwise it is left in the current room and the response is `You put it down.`. `examine NAME` with an item that is neither carried nor visible: `There is no {X} here.`. `inv`: `You carry: a, b` (ascending byte order) or `You carry nothing.`

**Darkness.** A dark room is *lit* when the player carries at least one light source (any item named by a `light` line); in a dark room that is not lit the room view is the single line `Pitch black.` (for `look` and after `go`). Moving is still allowed. `score` responds `Score: N`, where `N` is the sum of the `value`s of all items currently lying in the rooms named by `vault` lines (an item without a `value` counts 0).

**State, undo and saves.** The state is the player's room, the carried items, where every item lies, and the move count (the number of successful `go` commands). Every *successful* `go`, `take`, `drop` and `load` first remembers the state before it, on a stack. `undo` pops that stack and restores the state (`Undone.`); with an empty stack it responds `Nothing to undo.` and nothing else happens. `turns` responds `Turns: N`. `save NAME` stores the current state under NAME (overwriting an older save) and responds `Saved.`; `load NAME` responds `No such save.` if there is none, otherwise it remembers the current state on the undo stack, restores the saved one and responds `Loaded.` (the save itself stays). Failed commands, `look`, `inv`, `score`, `turns`, `save` and `undo` do not touch the stack.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/adventure.js`:

```
function adventure(world, script)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `world`: the world description text
* `script`: the command script, one command per line
* returns the transcript, or a world error text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  desc hall A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  look
  go north
  go north
  look
result:
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  A cold hall with a dusty floor.
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > go north
  You can't go that way.
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
```

**Example 2**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item rope yard a coil of rope
script:
  take lamp
  examine lamp
  go north
  look
  take rope
  inv
  drop lamp
result:
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > examine lamp
  a brass lamp
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > look
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  Items: rope
  > take rope
  You pick it up.
  > inv
  You carry: lamp, rope
  > drop lamp
  You put it down.
```

**Example 3**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room vault Vault
  exit hall east vault
  exit vault west hall
  item key hall an iron key
  lock hall east key
  start hall
script:
  go east
  take key
  go east
  drop key
  go west
  go east
result:
  > go east
  The door is locked.
  > take key
  You pick it up.
  > go east
  == Vault ==
  Exits: west
  > drop key
  You put it down.
  > go west
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: east
  > go east
  The door is locked.
```

**Example 4**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room cave Cave
  exit hall down cave
  exit cave up hall
  item lamp hall a brass lamp
  item coin cave a silver coin
  light lamp
  dark cave
  vault hall
  value coin 25
  start hall
script:
  go down
  look
  go up
  take lamp
  go down
  look
  take coin
  go up
  drop coin
  score
result:
  > go down
  Pitch black.
  > look
  Pitch black.
  > go up
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: down
  Items: lamp
  > take lamp
  You pick it up.
  > go down
  == Cave ==
  Exits: up
  Items: coin
  > look
  == Cave ==
  Exits: up
  Items: coin
  > take coin
  You pick it up.
  > go up
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: down
  > drop coin
  You put it down.
  > score
  Score: 25
```

**Example 5**

```
world:
  room hall Entrance Hall
  room yard Back Yard
  exit hall north yard
  exit yard south hall
  start hall
script:
  save here
  go north
  turns
  undo
  look
  go north
  load here
  turns
  undo
  turns
  undo
result:
  > save here
  Saved.
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > turns
  Turns: 1
  > undo
  Undone.
  > look
  == Entrance Hall ==
  Exits: north
  > go north
  == Back Yard ==
  Exits: south
  > load here
  Loaded.
  > turns
  Turns: 0
  > undo
  Undone.
  > turns
  Turns: 1
  > undo
  Undone.
```
